I farm the way I have been doing for years, but I still adjust a little when I see a better result nearby. On my 6 mu, wheat and maize are one chain. If I spend too little on wheat, the stand is weak and I lose grain. If I spend too little on maize, the ears stay small. I do not like taking big risks, so I will follow the usual wheat-maize pattern and keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, because losing yield hurts more than spending some extra money. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the main fertilizer down before sowing, and then topdress nitrogen at jointing. I will water about 3 times if the year is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, put base fertilizer at sowing, then chase nitrogen around the big-bell stage, and water about 2 times. On 6 mu, I still do careful counting, because every bag costs money, but I will not cut back too hard on fertilizer or seed. I will keep tillage simple with rotary work after each harvest because it saves labor and is what many people around me do. I expect stable yields if weather is not bad and pests do not flare up too much.
